headline: A Common Sense Media study rated Google's AI search answers unsafe for children and teenagers, and Google called the study flawed.
score_reason: Widely used product and a credible child-safety group with hard numbers, but a single advocacy study that Google disputes and no regulatory action.
importance_line: Children who use Google's AI answers on school laptops may get poor responses in a crisis, which puts parents, teachers and school districts in the position of managing the risk, though Google says the test queries were contrived and its own checks gave better results.
summary: Mashable reports that Common Sense Media's Youth AI Safety Institute, after about 2,600 test interactions on accounts set up as 11- and 15-year-olds, concluded that Google's AI Overview and AI Mode are an "unacceptable risk" for minors, finding they offered a hotline or medical referral in only 58 and 77 percent of the 214 crisis prompts that needed one. Google told Mashable the queries were "ambiguous and contrived" and that it could not reproduce many results; the group wants the features switched off by default for minors, three-quarters of whom it says use Google's AI answers.
notes: Mashable's own reporting with statements from both sides.
